title: Maps into shifted character-dual free DG modules compute dual cohomology
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbf Z}A^j$ be an associative unital differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$: $d_A$ has degree $1$, $d_A^2=0$, and $d_A(ab)=d_A(a)b+(-1)^j a\,d_A(b)$ for $a\in A^j$. A right DG $A$-module $M$ is a graded right module with a degree-$1$ differential satisfying $d_M^2=0$ and $d_M(ma)=d_M(m)a+(-1)^j m\,d_A(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Use shifts $M[k]^n=M^{n+k}$ with differential $(-1)^k d_M$ and unchanged right action. Write $(A^\vee)^n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(A^{-n},\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$, with $(d\lambda)(a)=(-1)^{n+1}\lambda(d_Aa)$ for $\lambda\in(A^\vee)^n$, and right action $(\lambda a)(b)=\lambda(ab)$. For the underlying cochain complex of abelian groups define $(M^\vee)^r=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(M^{-r},\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z)$ and $(d_{M^\vee}\lambda)(m)=(-1)^{r+1}\lambda(d_Mm)$. Put $H^r(M^\vee)=\ker d_{M^\vee}^r/\operatorname{im}d_{M^\vee}^{r-1}$. Let $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{DG}(A)}(X,Y)$ denote the group of degree-zero right $A$-linear chain maps, and let $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(X,Y)$ be its quotient by chain homotopy: $f\sim f^{\prime}$ when $f-f^{\prime}=d_Yh+hd_X$ for a degree-$-1$ right $A$-linear additive map $h$. For every integer $k$, evaluation $f\mapsto(m\mapsto f(m)(1))$ induces natural isomorphisms of abelian groups $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{DG}(A)}(M,A^\vee[k])\cong\ker(d_{M^\vee}:(M^\vee)^k\to(M^\vee)^{k+1}),\qquad\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(M,A^\vee[k])\cong H^k(M^\vee).$$ In the evaluation formula $m\in M^{-k}$. These isomorphisms are contravariantly natural in all right DG $A$-modules $M$, without any boundedness, acyclicity or finiteness assumption.

source.place: Tag 09K4, lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free, both displayed natural identifications.

proof.text:
Set $Y=A^\vee[k]$ and write $D=M^\vee$. First $d_A1=0$: the Leibniz identity at $1\cdot1$ gives $d_A1=2d_A1$. The displayed dual differential squares to zero since it is a signed precomposition with $d_A^2=0$. For $\alpha\in(A^\vee)^n$, $a\in A^j$ and $b\in A^{-n-j-1}$, the Leibniz rule gives
$$(d(\alpha a))(b)=(-1)^{n+j+1}\alpha(a\,d_Ab)=( (d\alpha)a+(-1)^n\alpha(d_Aa))(b).$$
Associativity of the right action is $((\alpha a)c)(b)=\alpha(acb)=(\alpha(ac))(b)$, and its unit is immediate. Thus the specified formulas really make $A^\vee$ a right DG module. Multiplying the differential by $(-1)^k$ verifies the DG rule for $Y$ with its unchanged action. The same square-zero check defines the complex $D$.

source.place: Tag 09K4, lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free; explicit expansion of the proof, using the preceding character-dual conventions.

proof.text:
For an integer $t$, let $G^t$ be the abelian group of degree-$t$ additive maps $\phi:M\to Y$ satisfying $\phi(ma)=\phi(m)a$, with no chain-map condition. Define $E_t:G^t\to D^{k+t}$ by $E_t(\phi)(m)=\phi(m)(1)$ for $m\in M^{-k-t}$. Its inverse is the explicit formula
$$F_t(\lambda)(m)(a)=\lambda(ma),\qquad m\in M^p,\quad a\in A^{-p-k-t}.$$
The degrees put $ma$ in $M^{-k-t}$ and $F_t(\lambda)(m)$ in $Y^{p+t}$. Additivity is termwise, and right linearity follows from $\lambda((mc)a)=\lambda(m(ca))$. Evaluation of $F_t(\lambda)$ at $1$ recovers $\lambda$. Conversely right linearity gives $\phi(m)(a)=(\phi(m)a)(1)=\phi(ma)(1)$, so $F_tE_t\phi=\phi$. These are inverse additive bijections.

source.place: Tag 09K4, lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free; explicit expansion of the proof, using the preceding character-dual conventions.

proof.text:
For $\phi\in G^t$ put $\delta\phi=d_Y\phi-(-1)^t\phi d_M$. Expanding both terms at $ma$ shows that the two terms involving $d_Aa$ have coefficients $(-1)^{p+t}$ and $-(-1)^{t+p}$; they cancel. Hence $\delta\phi\in G^{t+1}$. For $m\in M^{-k-t-1}$, the $d_Y\phi$ term evaluates to zero at $1$, since $d_A1=0$. Consequently
$$E_{t+1}(\delta\phi)(m)=(-1)^{t+1}E_t(\phi)(d_Mm)=(-1)^k(d_D E_t(\phi))(m),$$
where $d_D$ in degree $k+t$ is $(-1)^{k+t+1}$ times precomposition with $d_M$. This proves the differential identity in every degree, including negative $k$ and $t$.

source.place: Tag 09K4, lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free; explicit expansion of the proof, using the preceding character-dual conventions.

proof.text: Take $t=0$ in step 3. The condition $\delta f=0$ is precisely $d_Yf=f d_M$, whereas $E_1(\delta f)=(-1)^k d_D E_0(f)$. Since $E_1$ is injective and multiplication by $(-1)^k$ is invertible, $E_0$ restricts to an additive bijection between degree-zero DG maps $M\to Y$ and $\ker(d_D:D^k\to D^{k+1})$. Its inverse is $F_0$ restricted to those cycles. This is the first asserted isomorphism, with exactly the stated evaluation formula.

source.place: Tag 09K4, lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free; explicit expansion of the proof, using the preceding character-dual conventions.

proof.text: Take $t=-1$ in step 3. A homotopy operator is precisely $h\in G^{-1}$, and $\delta h=d_Yh+h d_M$. The formula reads $E_0(\delta h)=(-1)^k d_D E_{-1}(h)$. Thus homotopic chain maps have evaluations differing by a boundary. Conversely if $E_0(f-g)=d_D\mu$ for $\mu\in D^{k-1}$, choose $h=F_{-1}((-1)^k\mu)$. The formula and injectivity of $E_0$ give $f-g=d_Yh+h d_M$. Therefore evaluation and $F_0$ descend to mutually inverse additive maps between the two quotients, namely $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A)}(M,Y)$ and $\ker d_D^k/\operatorname{im}d_D^{k-1}=H^k(D)$.

source.place: Tag 09K4, lemma-hom-into-shift-dual-free; explicit expansion of the proof, using the preceding character-dual conventions.

proof.text: For a DG map $u:N\to M$, and $n\in N^{-k-t}$, evaluation gives $E_t(\phi u)(n)=\phi(u(n))(1)=(E_t(\phi)\circ u)(n)$. The inverse formula also commutes with $u$, because $u(na)=u(n)a$. Precomposition commutes with the differentials since $u$ is a chain map, and sends $d_Yh+h d_M$ to $d_Y(hu)+(hu)d_N$. Hence these equalities pass both to cycles and to the quotients in step 5. They prove contravariant naturality of both isomorphisms. Every formula is degreewise and uses no infinite sum, boundedness, finiteness, or acyclicity hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem shiftedCharacterDualHom (A : Algebra.{u}) (k : ℤ) : ∃ (E : ∀ M : RightModule A, characterDualMaps A M k ≃+ characterDualCycles ((underlying A).obj M) k) (F : ∀ M : RightModule A, CharacterDualHomotopyMaps A M k ≃+ CharacterDualCohomology ((underlying A).obj M) k), (∀ (M : RightModule A) (f : characterDualMaps A M k) (m : ((underlying A).obj M).X (-k)), (E M f).val m = f.val (-k) m ((A.X.XIsoOfEq (show (0 : ℤ) = -(-k + k + 0) by omega)).hom (characterDualUnit A))) ∧ (∀ (M : RightModule A) (f : characterDualMaps A M k), F M (QuotientAddGroup.mk' (characterDualNullMaps A M k) f) = QuotientAddGroup.mk' (characterDualBoundaries ((underlying A).obj M) k) (E M f)) ∧ (∀ (M N : RightModule A) (u : N ⟶ M) (f : characterDualMaps A M k) (g : characterDualMaps A N k) (_hg : ∀ (p : ℤ) (n : ((underlying A).obj N).X p), g.val p n = f.val p ((((underlying A).map u).f p) n)) (n : ((underlying A).obj N).X (-k)), (E N g).val n = (E M f).val ((((underlying A).map u).f (-k)) n))
